status: pre-registered after a smoke (French items only, top 4 rows; SmolLM2 on 4 windows), before the full run
question: Cammarata 2026 read with e661: do the attribute relay rows have signed two-pole structure that e661's |activation| hid, is generation two-poled rather than absent, and how common is the SwiGLU gate-closed double-negative leak at the top of a neuron's positive activations (the essay: about 4% of Qwen3 neurons)?
design: Part A: Qwen2.5-0.5B, e622/e659 translation items (French, Spanish, German) via wdd_demo's harness; the top 8 direct-contribution rows of gender, number and generation; each pole's signed mean activation at the word, the regime shares (gate open positive, gate open negative, gate closed positive = double negative, gate closed negative), the gate-closed share of |a|. Part B: Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2-135M, every MLP neuron, wikitext-2 windows of 256 tokens (128 windows, about 33k positions; a snapshot after 16 windows); each neuron's top-20 positive and negative activations and their regimes; a neuron is leak-dominated when more than half of its top-20 positive activations are gate-closed.

hypotheses.S1: Cammarata's figure at our scale: at about 33k wikitext positions, between 0.01 and 0.10 of MLP neurons are leak-dominated, in both Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2-135M
hypotheses.S2: the leak-dominated share falls with more text: lower at about 33k positions than at about 4k, in both models
hypotheses.S3: signed poles: at least half of the 16 top gender and number rows have opposite-signed mean activations on the two poles
hypotheses.S4: generation is two-poled, not absent: at least 2 of its top 8 rows have opposite-signed pole means with the smaller at least a quarter of the larger
hypotheses.S5: the leak is small at the word: the median gate-closed share of the relay rows' |activation| is under 0.2 for all three attributes
